question: T12 (task-3a0edc5b392a8307): the desktop rows after a Wave Intensity fall of two steps or more from a line that ran over its rows, and after a Text Size fall. On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a second block added after it (a second Scrolling block, or a Text block in HB and IB), made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/26 or 1/2/3/10; phone 1/2/3/10 and 3/2/5/10), so the section follows the desktop on the phone. Select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design ('open'), presses on Wave Intensity (179 is the press at the range's end, read as 180) or on a Text Size button, a read 1.3 s after each, 'go' (the selection left), then Cmd+Z ('Z'). HA: 150, 60, 0 (CAP-T12SHORT H again). HB: HA with a Text block. HC: 180, 90, 30. HD: 180, 90, 0. HE: 120, 60, 0. IB: 150, Large, Medium, Small with a Text block (CAP-T12SHORT I with a Text block). HP and HQ (the Scrolling block placed 1/2/3/26 by hand after 120 or 180) stopped at the placing: the oracle left it 1/2/5/26.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: A fall of two steps or more (60 px or more) on the desktop moves the block's foot up by the fall and snaps it down to the row pitch (CAP-T12WAVEDROP), only while the block has more rows than the new line needs; with no more than that its rows stay. H's 0 after 150 and 60 (2 rows, a 94 line running over them, to a 34 line that needs 2 rows): 1/2/3/26 stays, in HA, HB (a Text block, no second Scrolling block) and HE (120, 60, 0), S1, S2 and S3 alike. HC's 30 and HD's 0 after 180 and 90 (3 rows, a 124 line, to a 64 or 34 line that needs 2): 1/2/2/26, as CAP-T12WAVEDROP B2's 90 to 30.

Rule A of CAP-T12WAVEDROP alone gives 1 row for H's 0 (94 - 60 over a pitch of 41.1 is under 1 row); it fits the other 19 desktop falls of two steps or more read in the T12 findings. A rule on the stretched pitch (the block's height and a gap over its rows) was written before HD and HD refuted it (it gave 3 rows).

A Text Size fall on the desktop takes the same rule: I's Large (1/2/10/26, a 337 line) to Medium (243) gives 1/2/7/26, not the 1/2/8/26 that holds the line, and Medium to Small (184) 1/2/5/26, not 1/2/6/26 (CAP-T12SHORT I, R3 and R4; IB, S1 and S3 alike). A block below follows as on a Wave fall: IB's Text block at 8/2/10/10 after Large goes up by the foot's 3 rows to 5/2/7/10 at Medium and stays there at Small, where it starts on the new foot.

Written as predictions before the reads (scratchpad predictions.txt): HB's 0 and HC's 30 tell a twin effect from the block's rows (no twin effect); HD tells the stretched-pitch rule from rule A with the rows kept. Cmd+Z gives back the areas as CAP-T12SHORT says (not those before the step). The oracle does not let a block be placed by hand shorter than its line (HP, HQ). Not read: a fall from 3 rows or more to a line that still needs them all, a Text Size fall under 60 px, the phone view.
